User goal (family): Coordinate worktrees and arbitrate target branch merges
API, service or dispatch: See registered worktrees and merge coordination, not an agent count: one path has one registration. Before edits, also call agent_list(scope="checkout", online=true); isolate in a task worktree when another session occupies that checkout or coverage is unknown, then commit and merge back under a lease. Host-scoped by default — the clones on this machine, the worktrees registered in each, what each agent said it is doing, and any live merge lease or queue. Pass scope "clone" with a worktree_path to narrow to one checkout, or scope "fleet" to see every host. Always pass your own worktree_path once you have registered, at any scope: it tells the Director you are still here, so polling this while you work keeps your registration alive instead of letting it expire out from under you. Call this before creating a worktree or picking up work, so you find out about a peer in the same clone before you collide with them rather than after. The `stale` list on each clone is agents that were reclaimed — a session the fleet saw end, or one that went quiet — so a worktree missing from `worktrees` but present there was abandoned rather than never used. Each worktree's `branch` and `head_sha` are what its agent last reported, never a live read (the Director has no access to any worktree), and `head_observed_at` says when that HEAD was reported; a heartbeat alone advances `heartbeat_at` but not the HEAD. Check live state with `git rev-parse HEAD`, and pass your current `head_sha` (and `branch`) together with your registered worktree_path to update the recorded snapshot. The default reply is a compact summary page (default 20 clones, your own checkout first when worktree_path is registered): per clone the registered worktrees with task clipped, live leases without reason/overlap, and `worktree_count`/`lease_count`/`stale_count`. When `truncated` is true, call again with `offset` = `next_offset`. Pass detail "full" for the complete entries (declared paths, lease reasons and overlap, stale rows); scope "clone" returns full entries by default. On a busy host, narrow the page to your repository with remote_url (any spelling of `git remote get-url origin`; matches every clone of that repository in the scope) and/or clone_dir (your `--git-common-dir`); both work before you register. Clones with no active or uncertain registration, no live lease and no registration retired in the last 24 hours are omitted (counted in `idle_omitted`); pass include_idle true to list them. Clones dormant past the archive window (default 14 days: nobody registered, no open merge request, no activity) are archived and hidden even from include_idle (counted in `archived_omitted`); pass include_archived true to list them. Archiving deletes nothing, and git_register on an archived clone revives the same clone (`clone_unarchived: true`). An uncertain registration whose owner stays offline for 5 minutes, or whose session ended, is abandoned automatically and frees its path.

API, service or dispatch: Announce that you are working in a git worktree, BEFORE you start changing files. Gather the facts with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`, `git branch --show-current` and `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git remote get-url origin`, then pass them here. Idempotent: calling it again refreshes your registration and its TTL, and re-registering the same path under a different user is allowed and reported as rebound. Registrations expire, so a long stretch without calling any git_* tool lets the Director assume you are gone and reclaim your worktree; every call that names your worktree_path counts as proof you are still there. The Director never reads your worktree: the branch and head_sha you pass are stored as a reported snapshot (listed with head_observed_at), so refresh them with git_list(worktree_path, head_sha, branch) after you commit or switch. worktree_path must be the checkout your session is bound to (agent_context_update moves it), except that a separate repository nested inside that checkout, such as a submodule, registers directly with its own clone_dir. A remote_url naming a different repository than the one recorded for a clone that has live registrations is refused (git_director_remote_mismatch), so a typo cannot re-home the clone.

API, service or dispatch: Give back a merge lease as soon as the merge is done or abandoned, so whoever is waiting can proceed — a lease you forget about blocks the branch until its TTL runs out. Pass request_id to release one request, or worktree_path to drop everything outstanding for that worktree. This is an agent report, never server-verified merge proof. To correct a completed merged report, pass a stable correction_id UUID and correction_reason with the replacement target_head_sha; this appends an audit record, preserves the original report and never reactivates the lease. Do not combine correction with deregister. API, service or dispatch: Import files atomically from one File Transfer JSON bundle, preserving original paths, bytes, scanner line numbers and per-file revisions. Create UTF-8 JSON {"version":1,"files":[{"path":"src/app.ts","content":"source text","sha256":"optional lowercase SHA-256 of the decoded bytes"}]}, upload with cxx transfer put FILE --ttl-seconds 3600 --json, then pass transfer_id. Entries are source by default. Screenshots and a11y exports go in the same bundle to refresh a capture set in one call: {"path":"shots/home.png","content_base64":"<base64 of the PNG>"} (kind defaults from the extension; binary needs content_base64, a11y entries must be JSON). Each entry has exactly one of content or content_base64. No archive extraction, symlinks or removals. Limits unchanged: 200 current files, 2 MiB/file, 50 MiB decoded/job; bundle transport max 64 MiB (base64 adds a third). Duplicate/colliding paths, invalid hashes, bad base64 and over-cap imports fail as a whole. The result lists every path with rev and `unchanged`; identical files are no-ops, so a full refresh only appends revisions for changed paths. Omitted paths stay unchanged. Split larger applications into jobs. Requires File Transfer enabled.

API, service or dispatch: Upload one file into a slop job at a project-relative path (e.g. `src/routes/+page.svelte`, `DESIGN.md`, `shots/home-dark-390.png`). Uploading an existing path creates the next revision (v2, v3, ...); identical bytes are a no-op. Pass text inline as `content` (max 256 KiB) or upload with `cxx transfer put FILE --ttl-seconds 3600 --json` and pass `transfer_id` (max 2 MiB per file, 200 files, 50 MiB per job). `kind`: `source` (default for text; the deterministic scan only reads web `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.html/.css/.scss/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.mdx`, `.swift`, `.qml` and C++ sources, other source files such as `.php`, `.kt` or `.xml` are skipped by it and only seen by the advisor of a full run, as the `coverage` of each run states), `screenshot` (png/jpg/webp; default for those extensions; full runs only) or `a11y` (JSON audit export with `{tool, findings: []}`; full runs only). Accessibility trees such as Playwright ariaSnapshot YAML belong in `source`; they are review evidence, not automated audit findings. `remove: true` drops the path from the current set (history stays). A `DESIGN.md` at the root is the design brief.

Returns the run summary and the full slop report (version 2: findings with id, rule, priority P0-P2, kind measured|review, location, evidence, message, remedy, acceptance, alternative), or `format: "markdown"` for a readable digest. `wait_seconds` (0-25) waits for a running run. API, service or dispatch: Start a run over the current files. `mode: "quick"` runs the deterministic slop scan over source files only (screenshots and description are ignored; seconds). `mode: "full"` runs the same scan and then has the server-hosted Fleet Advisor review sources, screenshots, a11y exports, description, the design guidelines and the quick report; its findings are validated by slop before they are recorded (locations must exist). Full runs take minutes, need a managed agent session and File Transfer enabled, and the advisor answer also reaches you as an ADVISOR/1 message. Results are kept per run; re-run after uploading new revisions. Source files with unsupported extensions are skipped by the deterministic scan: the run `coverage` then lists the skipped and the covered extensions and states that those files got only the advisor review in a full run and none in a quick run. `client_message_id` (UUID) makes retries idempotent. `wait_seconds` (0-25, default 20 for quick) waits for the result.

Pass the bytes base64-encoded in `content_b64`, a display `name`, and `ttl_seconds` -- which is REQUIRED, because every transfer expires.
